#### Cumulative residual standard deviation plot {#sec-pri-628}

[**Purpose**]{#sec-pri-628-cumulativeressd}

The [cumulative residual standard deviation plot](#sec-pri-599) is used to identify the best (parsimonious) model.

[**Sample Cumulative Residual Standard Deviation Plot**]{#sec-pri-628-cumressdplot}

```{r}
#| label: fig-pri-628-cumressd
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative residual standard deviation plot for the sonoluminescent light intensity data"
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

sono <- read_table(
  here::here("datasets", "INN.DAT"),
  skip = 25,
  col_names = c("y", "x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5", "x6", "x7"),
  col_types = "dddddddd"
) |>
  mutate(
    x1x3 = x1 * x3, x2x3 = x2 * x3, x1x2 = x1 * x2, x3x4 = x3 * x4,
    x1x4 = x1 * x4, x2x4 = x2 * x4, x1x5 = x1 * x5, x1x2x4 = x1 * x2 * x4
  )

term_order <- c(
  "AVERAGE", "2", "7", "13", "1", "3", "23", "12",
  "34", "14", "6", "5", "124", "4", "24", "15"
)
predictors <- c(
  "x2", "x7", "x1x3", "x1", "x3", "x2x3", "x1x2",
  "x3x4", "x1x4", "x6", "x5", "x1x2x4", "x4", "x2x4", "x1x5"
)
formulas <- c("1", accumulate(predictors, ~ paste(.x, .y, sep = " + ")))
rsd_vals <- map_dbl(formulas, function(f) {
  s <- summary(lm(as.formula(paste("y ~", f)), data = sono))$sigma
  if (is.na(s)) 0 else s
})

cum_data <- tibble(term = factor(term_order, levels = term_order), rsd = rsd_vals)

ggplot(cum_data, aes(term, rsd)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = term, xend = term, y = 0, yend = rsd)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Sonoluminescent Light Intensity", subtitle = "Cumulative Residual SD Plot",
    x = "Cumulative Model", y = "Residual SD"
  ) +
  theme_light()
```

The plot shows the full cumulative sequence of all 15 terms, continuing past $X_1 X_2$ down to the saturated (perfect-fit, residual SD = 0) model; the discussion below, however, only concerns the first 7 terms (through $X_1 X_2$), since that is where NIST's own stopping rule applies.

[**Conclusions from the Cumulative Residual SD Plot**]{#sec-pri-628-conclusions}

We can make the following conclusions from the cumulative residual standard deviation plot.

1. The baseline model consisting only of the average ($\hat{Y}$ = 110.6063) has a high residual standard deviation (95).

   ```{r}
   #| code-fold: true
   round(rsd_vals[1], 2)
   ```

2. The cumulative residual standard deviation shows a significant and steady decrease as the following terms are added to the average: $X_2$, $X_7$, $X_1 X_3$, $X_1$, $X_3$, $X_2 X_3$, and $X_1 X_2$. Including these terms reduces the cumulative residual standard deviation from approximately 95 to approximately 17.

   ```{r}
   #| code-fold: true
   round(rsd_vals[8], 2)
   ```

3. Exclude from the model any term after $X_1 X_2$ as the decrease in the residual standard deviation becomes relatively small.
4. From the [|effects| plot](#sec-pri-626), we see that the average is 110.6063, the estimated $X_2$ effect is -78.6126, and so on. (The model coefficients are one half of the effect estimates.) We use this to form the following prediction equation:

   $$\begin{aligned}
   \hat{Y} & = 110.6063 - 39.3063 X_2 - 39.0563 X_7 + \\
           & \phantom{=} 35.00625 X_1 X_3 + 33.106245 X_1 + 31.90625 X_3 - \\
           & \phantom{=} 31.7313 X_2 X_3 - 29.781 X_1 X_2
   \end{aligned}$$

   ::: {.callout-note}
   NIST's original text and equation state the sixth term here as "$X_1 X_5$" with coefficient -31.7313. This is inconsistent with the cumulative model-building order given one sentence earlier in this same section ($X_2$, $X_7$, $X_1 X_3$, $X_1$, $X_3$, $X_2 X_3$, $X_1 X_2$ -- which has no $X_1 X_5$ term at all), and the coefficient -31.7313 is exactly half of the $X_2 X_3$ effect (-63.4625) established on [the |effects| plot page](#sec-pri-626) -- not the $X_1 X_5$ effect, which is only -0.5625. We give the term as $X_2 X_3$ above, consistent with the rest of this section.
   :::

   Note that $X_1 X_3$ is confounded with $X_2 X_7$ and $X_4 X_6$, $X_2 X_3$ is confounded with $X_4 X_5$ and $X_1 X_7$, and $X_1 X_2$ is confounded with $X_3 X_7$ and $X_5 X_6$.

   From the above graph, we see that the residual standard deviation for this model is approximately 17.
